title: HSNO Act Changes Unlikely to Pass Before November Election
description_clean: Changes to an act of parliament seen as critical to speeding up access to overseas products to control pests and invasive species in NZ is unlikely to get passed before the November election. The Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Amendment Bill, also known as the HSNO Act, has fallen victim to a huge raft of other legislation that the Government wants passed ahead of the bill in the current parliamentary term. The amendments to the HSNO Act are seen as a major priority by the primary sector, frustrated by red tape, long timeframes, complexity of the process, costs and overall uncertainty
summary: Changes to New Zealand's Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Act, aimed at speeding access to overseas pest-control products, are unlikely to pass before the November election due to competing legislation. The primary sector considers the amendments a priority amid frustration over red tape, timeframes, costs and uncertainty.
